nodes.label: Fleet calendar per-day pricing (Turo-style manual day prices)
Batch-load base rates + day prices in two queries, not per-vehicle
limit(5000) set well above fleet×range to dodge the PostgREST default row cap
Portal-set day prices land on the same table booking reads, so they apply at checkout
Fleet-level and per-vehicle daily-price caches must be invalidated together
Manual per-day price overrides base rate and surcharges for that day
Gig-driver proof image capability (list, upload, delete)
Storage path convention tenantId/customerId/timestamp-sanitisedName in gig-driver-images bucket
Read filters on customer_id only — tenant isolation is delegated entirely to RLS
Global cross-entity search palette (250ms debounce, keyboard navigation)
Ten searchable entity buckets: customers, vehicles, rentals, fines, payments, plates, insurance, invoices, insurances, agreements
Tenant currency is part of the search cache key because results are money-formatted
Tenant-initiated go-live approval request per integration
getRequestStatus only ever reports 'pending' — approved/rejected collapse to null
Module-level singleton Google Maps Places loader shared by every consumer
mounted ref guards setState after unmount on a promise that outlives the component
INSHUR/ABI integration configuration, mode and credential state
Tri-state T|null convention: null means 'we could not determine this', never 'no'
Bonzah balance card collapsed a failed lookup into a genuine zero and sent operators to top up a funded account
Bonzah balance hook conflates error and zero into one falsy value
Credentials are reduced to booleans inside the queryFn so secrets never reach the React Query cache
Client normalizeMode must mirror _shared/inshur-client.ts exactly or the UI labels a live tenant as simulating
Server-side INSHUR mode normalisation
Simulated insurance while Stripe is live — the renter pays for cover that does not exist
Without inshur_states_synced_at an empty states array is 'never asked', not 'covers nothing'
Every verification outcome is HTTP 200 with ok:false — a rejected credential is an answer, not a transport failure
Mock mode needs no credentials, which is what makes the whole flow exercisable before INSHUR hands anything over
INSHUR Period Z rental coverage lifecycle (create, end, cancel, retry)
source_mode is stamped at write time and never re-derived — a row created in simulation stays simulated forever
ABI publishes no webhooks, so a pending row is polled every 5s as the only completion signal
refetchOnWindowFocus overrides the global false because operators tab out to portal.abiweb.com and come back
No coverage id crosses the wire — the server resolves the live row itself to protect ABI's one-active-period-per-VIN invariant
pending and active are the two statuses the partial unique index treats as occupying the rental
Toast title branches on the mode the row was written in, not on whether the call succeeded
end-coverage says already_ended, cancel-coverage says already_settled — reading one spelling titled a no-op as an action
The coverage functions refuse requests with HTTP 200 plus an error field, so a clean invoke() is not evidence of cover
ABI refuses DELETE once the period has started, so a late cancel is routed to end server-side
Retry re-enters the same create function with force:true because the duplicate guard belongs on the server side of the wire
The rental-detail coverage block keeps its own cache of the same rows under a different key
Fleet-wide head count of rentals currently on cover, null when the count could not be taken
Per-vehicle INSHUR Period X eligibility verdict cache
A verdict older than 7 days is shown as stale because operators can add or remove a VIN from Period X silently
Four eligibility states, not two — 'unchecked' and 'unknown' are different problems with different fixes
check_failed and not_checked arrive with eligible:false but are not verdicts — flattening them accuses ABI of a rejection it never made
Fleet eligibility roll-up with per-reason buckets (needs Period X, no tracker, no comp/coll, no VIN, unchecked, stale, simulated)
Every fleet count is number|null so a failed read never renders as '0 vehicles eligible' — the failure mode inherited from the Bonzah balance card
Either half missing fails the whole query, so callers show 'unavailable' rather than a plausible zero
INSHUR identifies vehicles by VIN only, so a VIN-less vehicle is its own bucket rather than an ineligible one
Disposed vehicles are excluded from the fleet denominator so readiness is not understated forever
A settings-level re-check-everything must send vehicle_ids in one call, not loop this mutation — the server owns the fan-out throttle
Four separate eligibility query keys must be invalidated together because the vehicles-list badge caches the same reads
Rental installment plan management (retry, cancel, mark paid)
Retry works by resetting the installment to 'scheduled' so the cron processor picks it up on its next cycle
Manual cash settlement path — marks an installment paid outside the Stripe webhook chain
PGRST116 (no plan row) is treated as 'no plan', not as a query failure
Realtime fan-in for an installment plan, its installments and its notification timeline
One socket invalidates keys owned by three different screens (rental detail, customer portal, settings preview)
Customer insurance policy register with search/status/expiry filters and stats
Pre-write validation: no overlapping policy period, policy number unique per customer
Expiry/start are date-only columns and must be read with parseLocalDate, never new Date()
Policies whose customer join came back empty are dropped client-side rather than rendered half-blank
AI insurance-document verification pipeline (upload, score, flag, attach to rental)
DB row is created before the upload so the storage path can be keyed by id; the row is deleted if the upload fails
AI verification is invoked fire-and-forget and progress is observed by polling the row every 2.5s until terminal
Attaching a verification to a rental back-fills customer_id from the rental row
Storage cleanup re-derives the object path by regex from the stored public URL
Vehicle key handover (giving/receiving) with condition photos, notes and odometer
Giving the key activates the rental only when approved AND payment fulfilled; receiving it closes the rental and frees the vehicle
Deposit hold is placed on the saved card at collection and released at return
Notification, deposit-hold and Tesla-sync failures are swallowed — a side effect must never block the handover itself
Handover rows are upserted onConflict rental_id,handover_type to survive double-clicks and races
Return odometer drives excess-mileage charge calculation and updates the vehicle's current mileage
Rental-level mileage and excess-rate overrides take precedence over the vehicle's own config
Tesla Fleet vehicles get a live Supercharger charge sync folded into the return summary
A single handover invalidates ~15 query keys spanning rentals, vehicles, payments, invoices and mileage
Undo clears handed_at and reverts an Active rental to Pending, but does not undo the deposit hold or the notifications
Handover query keys omit the tenant id, unlike the leads/INSHUR convention
Single lead record for the lead workspace, kept fresh by a filtered realtime channel
Leads module implementation spec (Sections 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 10.3, 15) cited by every lead hook
Lead activity timeline — read-only event feed with system/staff/lead/ai actors
Lead kanban board — one query over the union of active stages, grouped into columns client-side
Lead document store with per-document verification status and expiry
Only leads and lead_activity get realtime; notes, documents and templates rely on a 30s staleTime
Lead stage transitions, assignment, tags and read tracking
canTransition() is validated client-side deliberately mirroring the DB trigger — two copies of one state machine
Optimistic stage update writes both the list caches and the single-lead cache, with full rollback on error
Contact edits are a thin passthrough so the normalise_lead_identifiers() trigger can recompute phone_normalised / email_lower
Mark-read is guarded by .eq('is_read', false) so re-opening a lead cannot overwrite the original reader and timestamp
Internal-only lead notes, pinned first — never sent to the lead
Per-tenant lead message templates (sms/email/whatsapp) for the composer's template picker
Lead writes filter only on id and lean on RLS for tenant scoping, while the reads still pin tenant_id
